transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I’m just really struggling with how hideous my face looks lately. I have these awful acne scars and my nose is so crooked and asymmetrical, and it's making me incredibly anxious. I just feel like my face looks completely deformed and I can't stop worrying about it.
How much time each day do you spend thinking about or checking these facial flaws, and does it interfere with your daily life?

I easily spend three to four hours every day constantly checking my skin and nose in the mirror, unable to stop thinking about how they look. It severely interferes with my life because I'm constantly late for work, and some days I can't even bring myself to go outside because I feel so self-conscious.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Body Dysmorphic Disorder, and the new information strongly supports it rather than changing the differential. The patient has a preoccupation with perceived facial defects, spends 3–4 hours daily checking, and has clear functional impairment with avoidance of work and going outside. No evidence was provided for an eating disorder, psychotic disorder, or mood/anxiety disorder as a better explanation, so the candidate list remains the same.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived facial defects (acne scars, crooked/asymmetrical nose) that are not described as objectively severe, spends 3–4 hours daily checking and ruminating, and has significant functional impairment with avoidance of work and going outside. This pattern is most consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder.
